February  2008 e-Menu
Dear  website members,
This  month, I'm giving you a preview of our new cookbook The Best Chicken 
  Recipes.  The book includes several specialty chapters with themes that many of 
  you  have requested, including Chicken Dinners for Two, Light and Lean Chicken, 
  and  Starting with Leftovers. My mostly make-ahead menu was inspired by the 
  leftover  chapter and includes instructions on roasting two chickens at the same 
  time  to create extra meat. (I've also added one of the test kitchen's all-time 
  favorite  cookie recipes.)
And  here are two tips for estimating how much meat to expect from a roasted 
  chicken:  Expect to get about 1 cup of shredded or thinly sliced cooked chicken 
  per  pound of raw chicken. But if you're purchasing an already cooked rotisserie 
  chicken  at the store, remember that chickens lose about 25 percent of their 
  weight  once cooked, so it will yield slightly more meat per pound than a raw 
  chicken.  Finally, most recipes for four people require 2 cups.
Enjoy!
Lindsay  McSweeney
  Online  Editor
